item.title: Skipper Cup: Taveuni captain credits growing fan support for team's rise
item.description: Speaking to fijivillage sports, Kamikamica says when he first captained the side two years ago, only a handful of supporters would visit the team during training camps and before matches. He says as the team continued to improve on the field, more people began believing in them and rallying behind their journey.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking to fijivillage sports, Kamikamica says when he first captained the side two years ago, only a handful of supporters would visit the team during training camps and before matches.

He says as the team continued to improve on the field, more people began believing in them and rallying behind their journey.

Kamikamica says that support has continued to grow, with villagers, Taveuni people living in Suva, other parts of Fiji and overseas all backing the team as they prepare for the Skipper Cup.

Insert:(VITIFM) Captain on community support

Kamikamica says travelling to competitions in Suva has never been easy, with the team relying on fundraising, kava barrel and donations from villages to cover the cost of travelling from the island.

He says the generosity of the community has helped keep the team's Skipper Cup dream alive and motivated the players to keep pushing through the challenges.

Kamikamica says the team is taking one game at a time, starting with Malolo this weekend, and is determined to give its best in every match.

He says faith has also played a big part in the team's preparation, with players praying together and trusting God to guide them through every challenge.

Kamikamica also thanked Northern Rally and Combat Sportswear for supporting the team with jerseys and training gear for this year's competition.

He also thanked his parents, siblings, wife and young child for standing by him as he prepares to lead Taveuni for a second straight season.

Kamikamica says his message to young people is to always give their best, be honest and never give up, even when it feels like nobody notices their efforts.

He says God sees every sacrifice and every struggle, and believes hard work will eventually be rewarded.

item.title: FIFA opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina after World Cup final defeat
item.description: FIFA has begun disciplinary action against Argentina following the team's behaviour during the 2026 FIFA World Cup final defeat by Spain and other incidents throughout the tournament. The world governing body last week appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess events after the final whistle at New York New Jersey Stadium, where several Argentina players and backroom staff were invol
item.content:encoded:
FIFA has begun disciplinary action against Argentina following the team's behaviour during the 2026 FIFA World Cup final defeat by Spain and other incidents throughout the tournament.

The world governing body last week appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess events after the final whistle at New York New Jersey Stadium, where several Argentina players and backroom staff were involved in altercations with Spain's players following the 1-0 defeat.

Following the prosecutor's recommendation, FIFA will investigate Argentina players Nahuel Molina, who faces two alleged assault charges, and Leandro Paredes, who faces three alleged assault charges, under Article 14 of FIFA's Disciplinary Code.

Argentina assistant coach Roberto Ayala also faces one alleged assault charge.

Molina is also being investigated for one count of alleged unsporting behaviour under Article 14.

Argentina's Thiago Almada and Spain midfielder Gavi have also been charged with alleged unsporting behaviour.

The Argentine Football Association is also facing disciplinary action for alleged breaches, including using a sporting event for non-sporting demonstrations, team misconduct, discrimination and racist abuse, and breaches of order and security at matches.

Under FIFA's Disciplinary Code, players and officials found guilty of unsporting conduct face a minimum one-match suspension, while assault offences carry a minimum three-match ban.

item.title: Team Fiji Boxer Daunakamakama to face Sri Lanka's Keshani Hansika tonight in Commonwealth Games 57kg quarter finals
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 29/07/2026 Team Fiji boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama will fight in the women's 57kg quarter-finals at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games tonight.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 29/07/2026

Team Fiji boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama will fight in the women's 57kg quarter-finals at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games tonight.

She will take on Sri Lanka's Keshani Hansika at 11.30pm.

Daunakamakama booked her place in the quarter-finals after defeating Ghana's Adelaide Dede Djabatey 5-0 in the round of 16.

In results from this morning, Anahira McCutchen finished sixth in the women's 50-metre freestyle, clocking a time of 25.53 seconds.

In other events involving Team Fiji, long-distance runner Yeshnil Karan will compete in the men's one-mile heats at 10.10pm, Kelera Mudunakaso will race in the women's 200-metre breaststroke heats at 9.30pm, and Sitiveni Konataci will compete in the men's discus throw F42–44/F61–64 final at 7.25am tomorrow.

Australia currently leads the medal tally with 35 gold, 18 silver, and 27 bronze, Canada is second with 13 gold, 10 silver, and 12 bronze, while England is third with 10 gold 18 silver, and 15 bronze.

item.content:encoded:
Vashist Muni College has booked its place in the Extra Fiji Secondary Schools Football Championship after a commanding 7-0 win over International Secondary School in the Southern Zone U19 qualifier.

The team produced a dominant performance to secure qualification for the national championship, which will be held in Labasa next month.

Vashist Muni College will now join the country's top secondary school teams as they compete for the national title in Labasa.

item.title: New Deans format sparks backlash over loyalty and player recruitment - Serevi
item.description: Former Fiji 7s Wizard and Legend Waisale Serevi has called on the Fiji Rugby Union and the organisers of the Vodafone Deans Competition to do away with the new Deans format, as it defeats the purpose and the loyalty students have for their school. Serevi highlighted this on his social media post following the review of the Terms of Participation, where teams that qualify for the national eliminati
item.content:encoded:
Former Fiji 7s Wizard and Legend Waisale Serevi has called on the Fiji Rugby Union and the organisers of the Vodafone Deans Competition to do away with the new Deans format, as it defeats the purpose and the loyalty students have for their school.

Serevi highlighted this on his social media post following the review of the Terms of Participation, where teams that qualify for the national eliminations, or quarter-finals, will be allowed to recruit up to six players from within their zone to strengthen their squads for the remainder of the competition.

Another concerned parent, Asenaca Blake, voiced her anger and says rugby was built on loyalty, discipline, commitment, and earning your jersey, not recruiting players once the hard work is done.

Blake says the new format teaches the boys that they are replaceable rather than loyalty.

She says winning should never come at the expense of character.

The mother of three says this rule is a step backwards, not forward.

Frustrations and mixed emotions across the nation as the new Deans format sparks criticism from spectators who did not like this format.

Looking at the Under-18 elimination matches, Lelean Memorial School will take on Marist Brothers High School, Suva Grammar School will face Ratu Luke Secondary School, Cuvu College will meet St John's College, Navatu Secondary School will play Ra High School, Ratu Kadavulevu School will face Ratu Sukuna Memorial School, Nasinu Secondary School will take on Holy Cross College, Ba Provincial Freebird Institute will meet Queen Victoria School, and Shri Guru Nanak Khalsa College will face Ratu Navula College.

item.title: Commonwealth Games: Heleina Young and Yeshnil Karan running tonight
item.description: Team Fiji athlete Heleina Young will be running in the 200 Metres Heats this evening at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games. The 200 Metres Heats starts from 9.30pm with Young in Heat 6.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji athlete Heleina Young will be running in the 200 Metres Heats this evening at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games.

The 200 Metres Heats starts from 9.30pm with Young in Heat 6.

Fiji’s long distance specialist, Yeshnil Karan will be participating in the Men's 1 Mile at 10.10pm.

Team Fiji will be in the Lawn Bowls Men's Pairs sectional at 7.30pm, while Elizabeth Moceiwai will be participating in the Single's Sectional at 10.20pm.

The Women's 200 Metres Breaststroke Heats has Kelera Mudunasoko competing at 9.30pm while the Men's 4x100 Metres Medley Relay Heats is at 10.52pm.

Boxing sensation, Jasmine Daunakamakama will be fighting in the Women's 57kg quarterfinals at 11.30pm.

Australia currently leads the medal tally with 35 gold, 18 silver, and 27 bronze, Canada is second with 13 gold, 10 silver, and 12 bronze, while England is third with 10 gold 18 silver, and 15 bronze.

item.title: Lautoka school football semi finals and finals kick off this Friday
item.description: The Lautoka Secondary Schools Soccer Association U19 Boys semi finals and finals, along with the Open Girls final, will be held this Friday at Churchill Park. The first U19 boys semi final will see Central College Lautoka take on Drasa Secondary from 9am .
item.content:encoded:
The Lautoka Secondary Schools Soccer Association U19 Boys semi finals and finals, along with the Open Girls final, will be held this Friday at Churchill Park.

The first U19 boys semi final will see Central College Lautoka take on Drasa Secondary from 9am .

The second semi final will be played from 10.20am , with Lautoka Muslim College facing Tilak High School.

The Open Girls final will kick off at 1pm , with Central College Lautoka taking on Pt. Vishnu Deo Memorial College.

The U19 Boys final will then be played from 2.20pm featuring the winners of the two semi finals.

The Lautoka Secondary Schools Soccer Association says all matches will be played at Churchill Park, with tickets priced at $3 for students in school uniform and $5 for all other spectators .

They are also calling on football fans, parents and supporters to turn out in numbers and cheer on their schools as the teams battle for this year's titles.
